# Introduction

In female mammalian cells one X chromosome is inactivated. Which one is
inactive differs from cell to cell, and it can be read from allele-specific
expression at heterozygous SNVs. **EXCISE** phases the heterozygous SNVs of
one chromosome into two haplotypes, X1 and X2, and calls each cell as `X1`,
`X2`, `Both` (biallelic), `Low_coverage` or `Unknown`.

EXCISE extends XCISE (Henning et al., bioRxiv 2024,
doi:10.1101/2024.08.29.610317). The package runs a C++ port of
`excise1.5.pl` that gives the same results, linked to htslib through
`r Biocpkg("Rhtslib")`.

# Installation

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("EXCISE")
```

# Input

EXCISE needs:

1.  A coordinate-sorted, indexed BAM file aligned with STAR in WASP mode
    (`--waspOutputMode SAMtag --outSAMattributes vA vG CB UB ...`). Reads
    need the WASP tags `vA`, `vG` and `vW`, a cell barcode in `CB` (or `RG`
    for plate-based data) and, if available, a UMI in `UB`.
2.  A VCF of heterozygous SNVs on the chromosome analysed (plain or
    gzipped).
3.  Optionally, a whitelist of cell barcodes, such as a 10x
    `barcodes.tsv.gz`.

The package contains a small simulated example: 300 cells and 200 SNVs on a
5 Mb chromosome `X`, with known cell states.

```{r files}
library(EXCISE)
bam <- system.file("extdata", "sim_chrX.bam", package = "EXCISE")
vcf <- system.file("extdata", "sim_chrX_hets.vcf", package = "EXCISE")
```

# Running EXCISE

```{r run}
res <- runExcise(bam, vcf, tries = 20, pretrain = TRUE, seed = 42)
res
```

`tries` is the number of optimiser restarts (default 100); `pretrain = TRUE`
starts each try from a co-segregation graph of the SNVs, which is
recommended. Use `workers` to run tries in parallel and `bamThreads` to read
the BAM in parallel.

# Results

Per-cell calls are a `DataFrame`. `hap1` and `hap2` are the UMIs supporting
haplotype X1 and X2.

```{r calls}
calls <- xciCalls(res)
head(calls)
table(calls$call)
```

The phased SNVs are a `GRanges`. `x1Allele` says which allele lies on X1;
`Unk` marks SNVs left unassigned, for example candidates for escape from
X inactivation.

```{r snvs}
xciSnvs(res)
table(xciSnvs(res)$x1Allele)
```

For simulated data the calls can be compared with the truth. The names X1 and
X2 are arbitrary, so the comparison allows them to be swapped.

```{r truth}
truth <- read.delim(
    system.file("extdata", "sim_chrX_truth.tsv", package = "EXCISE"),
    header = FALSE, col.names = c("barcode", "state"))
pred <- as.character(calls$call)[match(truth$barcode, calls$barcode)]
table(truth = truth$state, EXCISE = pred)
```

# Adding calls to a SingleCellExperiment

```{r sce}
library(SingleCellExperiment)
bc <- calls$barcode
sce <- SingleCellExperiment(assays = list(
    counts = matrix(0L, 2, length(bc), dimnames = list(c("g1", "g2"), bc))))
sce <- addXciCalls(sce, res)
table(sce$xci_call)
```

# Files compatible with excise1.5.pl

With `outPrefix`, `runExcise()` also writes the five files of `excise1.5.pl`
(`*_bc2xci.txt`, `*_summary.txt`, `*_XCISE.vcf`, `*_haplotypes.tsv` and
`*_cell_snv_profile.tsv`) in the same format, for existing downstream scripts.

```{r files-out}
out <- file.path(tempdir(), "example")
res <- runExcise(bam, vcf, tries = 20, pretrain = TRUE, seed = 42,
    outPrefix = out)
list.files(tempdir(), pattern = "^example_chrX_XCISE")
```

# Choosing parameters

The two filters that matter most are `minUmis` (minimum UMIs per SNV, default
4) and `penalty` (score penalty per discordant UMI, default 5). In simulations
the defaults were close to the best setting at standard coverage, at low
coverage and with sparse SNVs. A very low penalty (1) phases escape SNVs and
turns many monoallelic cells into `Both`. A very high penalty (12 or more)
leaves many SNVs unassigned and, on sparse data, can assign cells to the wrong
X. A high `minUmis` only matters when SNVs have few UMIs, where it removes
evidence.
